classification.difficultyReason: Connect the equality f(-x)=f(x) for distinct opposite inputs to repeated outputs and hence failure of the inverse to be a function.

content.prompt: Explain why the inverse of an even function will not be a function.

answer.short: For a nonzero $x$ in the domain, an even function satisfies $f(-x)=f(x)$. Thus two distinct inputs have the same output, so the function fails the horizontal line test and its inverse is not a function.
answer.worked: An even function satisfies $f(-x)=f(x)$. For a nonzero $x$ in its domain, $x$ and $-x$ are distinct inputs with the same output. The horizontal line through that output meets the graph at least twice. Its inverse therefore fails the vertical line test and is not a function.
